What each part of the screen means.

book.edgerunner.guide.cyberpsychosis.ove: Cyberpsychosis is the mind breaking under too much chrome. The more pressure you carry, the more humanity you lose. With little humanity left come symptoms and, in the end, episodes.

book.edgerunner.guide.cyberpsychosis.dia: Using it
Aim at someone close to examine them; with nobody in front, it examines you. It shows their chrome, their load and the state of their mind.
Load bar
The bar at the top is your capacity and fills with your implants' load. The number is load used / capacity. If it turns red you are overloaded and pressure rises.
IMMUNO
With immunosuppressants the bar grows: the light green part above the small notch is borrowed capacity. IMMUNO 12:30 is the time it has left; then that room is gone.
Saturation healing
SATURATION HEALING shows how well food heals you compared with a body without chrome. It drops as your permanent capacity fills and stops when it is full.
Body slots
Around the body are the slots: cortex, OS, arms, face, skeleton, hands, nerves, blood, skin and legs. Hover an implant to read it. Suppressors shows the doses kept in that slot.
Humanity
HUMANITY is how much of you is left, in percent. It drops while pressure is high and recovers when it calms down. Below it you see CLEAR or your stage; ORGANIC with no chrome.
Pressure
PRESSURE is the strain of the moment. Overload raises it, and so does using Sandevistan, Berserk, Gorilla Arms, the optics scan or the Blood Pump. Immunosuppressants lower it.
Trend and control
RISING, FALLING or STEADY tells where pressure is heading. In red you may read PARANOIA, LOSING CONTROL or EPISODE IMMINENT: time to get away from people and treat yourself.
Symptom list
The list on the right shows the symptoms you can suffer in your current state, not a history. NO SYMPTOMS means there is no risk for now.
book.edgerunner.guide.cyberpsychosis.man: Do not run several pressure-raising implants at once and stay within your capacity. If you are overloaded, remove chrome at a ripperdoc.
Each dose gives extra capacity for a while and lowers pressure. Keep them in the Suppressors slot of the ripperdoc, up to 16, so you have them when you need them.
book.edgerunner.guide.cyberware.skeleton: Skeleton implants that help you move: more speed, better jumps, softer landings and bounces. Pick the ones that suit how you get around.
Hollow Bones cannot be combined with Titanium Bones or Dense Marrow. Kinetic Frame pauses while Scarab is defending. Each entry tells its own load.
Skeleton implants for fighting up close: more damage, more resistance in combat, the Slam and the planted defence of Scarab.
They stack with arm implants such as Gorilla Arms or Mantis Blades. Check each entry for its load and what it does to your pressure.
Skeleton implants for staying alive: resistances, recovery, relief from pressure and help when your health is low.
Resistances from different implants share a common cap, so stacking them all does not make you immune. Each entry says what it adds.
book.edgerunner.guide.cyberware.microgen: Electric shots after reloading. Needs TacZ.

Charges the bullets of TacZ guns. Reload an empty gun and the next shot sets off an electric discharge on impact.

Without the TacZ mod, the implant cannot be crafted and does not appear in the game.
The discharge deals 2 hearts within 2 blocks and is ready again after 8 s. Fully upgraded it deals 4 hearts within 3 blocks every 6 s.
Tier 2: craft it at the assembly bench and have a ripperdoc install it in your hands. It adds 10 load, up to 22 with every upgrade.
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.we: What this mod is and how to use the guide.
This mod adds cyberware: implants that give you powers such as slowing time, blades in your arms or seeing enemies through walls. Every implant takes room in your body and puts pressure on your mind.

1. Craft a **RipperDoc**.
2. Build an implant at the assembly bench.
3. Install it sitting in the RipperDoc.
4. Use it and watch your load.

**Getting started** covers the basics. **Implants** has one entry per implant: what it does, how to use it and how to get it. **Cyberpsychosis** explains what happens to your mind and how to keep control.
Craft a new one with a book and two iron ingots. Entries open in order: start at the top of each tab and follow the lines down.
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.ri: The chair where implants go in and out.
A 3x3 surgery chair. While you hold it you see the space it needs: white if it fits, red if something is in the way.
Right-click the RipperDoc to sit down and open surgery. Drag each implant into its body slot to install it, or take it out to remove it. Close the screen to stand up; the changes apply then.
Each body part has its own slots: OS, cortex, face, arms, hands, circulatory, skeleton, nervous system, skin and legs, plus one for immunosuppressants. An implant only fits the slot of its body part.
The surgery screen shows your load bar, how fast food heals you and a preview of your body. Drag the preview to turn it and use the wheel to zoom.
An unemployed villager near a RipperDoc takes it as a workstation and becomes a ripperdoc trader. See «Ripperdoc villager».
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.in: What to prepare and what to pick first.
Pick an implant that fits your capacity. Bring food and another way to heal: with implants, food heals you more slowly. Basic Kiroshi Optics on your face let you read cyberware data.
Start with tier 1 implants: they need simple parts and little load. Every entry in the Implants tab tells its tier, its load and what it needs.
The implant starts adding load straight away. Some work on their own; others are used with the ability keys. See «Using your implants».
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.pa: A bench to paint implants. While you hold it you see the space it needs: white if it fits, red if not.
Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Blood Pump, legs, operating systems and optics. Optics paint a layer over the face of your skin.
Right-click it and put the implant in the left slot. Paint on the 3D model: left click paints, right click erases and the wheel zooms. Save to store the design on the item.
Save designs as named presets to reuse them. Import and Export share designs with others. Revert goes back to the last design saved on the item.
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.ab: Active implants use the ability keys. Each key is a zone: OS $(k:key.palladium.ability_1), arms $(k:key.palladium.ability_2), face $(k:key.palladium.ability_3), circulatory $(k:key.palladium.ability_4) and extra $(k:key.palladium.ability_5). You can change them in Controls; this guide shows your current keys.
Many implants need no key and work on their own while installed. Each entry in the Implants tab says whether it is used with a key or not.
Each implant has an upgrade tree in the Powers screen, opened from the inventory. Upgrades cost Internal Parts and raise the implant load: hover one to see the change before buying.
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.ca: How much chrome your body takes.
Every implant has a **load**. Your **capacity** is how much load you can carry. The RipperDoc bar shows both: if load goes over capacity the bar turns red and you are **overloaded**.
The first time you join a world you get a random capacity between 160 and 320. It stays yours in that world. Capacity upgrades in the Cyberware tree raise it, up to x1.50 at the last level.
While overloaded, cyberpsychosis pressure rises faster. Remove implants or take immunosuppressants to get back under your capacity.
Buying upgrades raises the load of that implant. Hover an upgrade to see how much it adds and how your bar will end up. A purchase can push you into overload, so check first.
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.im: Injectors that calm your body down so it rejects chrome less. Each dose gives you extra capacity for a while.
One dose adds 30%% to your capacity for 30 minutes and calms cyberpsychosis for a moment. That extra room is temporary: it does not speed up healing with food.
Right-click with them in hand to inject a dose. You can also install up to 16 doses in their RipperDoc slot and inject with the extra ability key ($(k:key.palladium.ability_5)).
The ripperdoc villager sells them from level 3. You can also craft them with the recipe on the next page.
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.he: Why you heal more slowly with implants.
With implants, food heals you more slowly. The more capacity you fill, the slower it gets: half full heals at half speed, and when it is full food stops healing. Hunger still refills.
The Blood Pump, potions and other healing work as usual. The RipperDoc screen shows how fast food heals you right now.
Craft a Hemo Chamber and a Biomonitor (next page) and assemble the Blood Pump at the assembly bench with the Soldering Iron.
A server can turn this rule off in the mod settings. If the world has natural regeneration off, food does not heal at all.
book.edgerunner.guide.getting_started.hu: The whole cyberware HUD needs optics on your face. Basic Kiroshi Optics are enough and work on their own.

Look at a creature to see its card. It reaches 24 blocks; holding the optics zoom ($(k:key.project_edgerunner.face_zoom)) at x4 takes it to 48. The $(k:key.project_edgerunner.optics_hud) key turns the card on or off.
Basic Kiroshi show health. Advanced optics scan to show more, such as effects or installed implants. The target must stay in sight while you scan.
Choose Full or Compact in the settings. Compact keeps small indicators and shows bigger cards in the normal inventory.
With Epic Fight, shaded cooldowns and charge fill stay visible on the bars. Its own icon leaves the cyberware slots free.
book.edgerunner.guide.crafting.ripperdoc: Sells the Soldering Iron, parts and immunosuppressants.
Place a RipperDoc near an unemployed villager and it takes the job. Trading with it raises its level and unlocks better offers.
Level 1: Soldering Iron. Level 2: Internal Parts T1 and T2. Level 3: T3 and immunosuppressants. Level 4: T4. Level 5: T5. Each trade asks for emeralds and one more material.
book.edgerunner.guide.crafting.soldering: The assembly bench tool for building implants. Crafting does not use it up.
The ripperdoc villager sells it from level 1, for 18 emeralds and 12 iron ingots. Buy it first: almost every implant needs it.
book.edgerunner.guide.crafting.internal_: Internal Parts, T1 to T5, pay for the upgrades of your implants and your capacity. The better the upgrade, the higher the part tier it asks for.
The ripperdoc villager sells them: T1 and T2 at level 2, then one more tier per level up to T5. Each costs emeralds plus redstone, quartz, diamonds, an ender eye or netherite scrap.
book.edgerunner.guide.crafting.crafting_: Implants are built at the Palladium Tailoring Bench, the assembly bench. Put the Soldering Iron in the tool slot, add the components the recipe asks for and take the implant.
Most implants need components that you craft first at a crafting table, such as the OS Frame T1 of the Sandevistan or the Arms Chassis T3 of the Gorilla Arms. Two examples follow.
config.project_edgerunner.catalog.sandev: 0-90%: how much slower Sandevistan users fall while it is active. Jumps keep their height. 0 = normal falling.

Each player sees the surgery sequence on their first qualifying operation (an OS install by default). Later surgeries are instant. Turn off to play it every time.

screen.project_edgerunner.blood_setup.le: A few drops and small stains (default).

Jets, pools and runs: a fight stays written on the floor.
